Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$\mathfrak p=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$ and $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
be as in [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]. Then:

**(1) (Simples.)** Within an integral block, $L(\lambda)\in\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
if and only if $\lambda$ is $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral; every simple
object of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is of this form.

**(2) (Standards.)** For $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the
generalized Verma $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$,
has finite length, has $L(\lambda)$ as its unique simple quotient (head), and
$[M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):L(\mu)]\neq0$ forces $\mu\le\lambda$ in the
dominance order; $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ is the largest quotient of
$M(\lambda)$ lying in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$.

**(3) (Enough projectives.)** The inclusion
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}\subseteq\mathcal O$ is exact and has a left adjoint
$L_{\mathfrak p}$ (the largest $\mathfrak p$-locally-finite quotient);
$L_{\mathfrak p}$ is right exact and sends projective objects of $\mathcal O$
to projective objects of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$. Consequently, for every
$\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the object
$P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=L_{\mathfrak p}(P^{(\mathcal O)}(\lambda))$ is a
projective cover of $L(\lambda)$ in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$, and
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ has enough projectives and injectives.

**(4) (Generalized-standard flags, BGG reciprocity and duality.)** Every
projective in a fixed integral block has a finite generalized Verma flag. Its
projective cover surjects to its labelled generalized standard with a kernel
filtered by higher-labelled generalized standards. The simple and
generalized-standard classes form bases of the finite block Grothendieck
group, and characters are injective on this group. For $\mathfrak p$-dominant
integral $\lambda,\mu$,
$$(P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=[M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$
the multiplicities being finite; moreover restricted duality restricts to an
exact contravariant involution of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ exchanging
$M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ and $\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$, and
$\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}}(M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda),\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=0$
for all $\lambda,\mu$.

p-finite (zero quotient is allowed). If K' is any other such kernel, M/(K∩K')
embeds in the finite product M/K⊕M/K', hence is p-finite. Minimality gives K⊂K'.
Therefore K is the intersection of all these kernels and gives the largest quotient
L_p M. This is a functor left adjoint to exact inclusion; it is right exact and
sends ordinary projectives to parabolic projectives. The quotient L_p P(η) maps
onto L(η) and this map is essential: the preimage in ordinary P(η) of any subobject
surjecting to L(η) is all of P(η). Thus it is the parabolic projective cover.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra with the standard parabolic $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak l\oplus\mathfrak u$, negative outside radical $\mathfrak v$, grading element $\zeta\in\mathfrak z(\mathfrak l)$, and the full locally $\mathfrak p$-finite subcategory $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ of ordinary $\mathcal O$. Write $N=U(\mathfrak v)$ and $B=U(\mathfrak p)$. The integral-block assertions are restricted to the integral central-character summands stated above.

[F1] Parabolic objects and Serre closure ([[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]], [[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]]): finite Levi simples $E(\lambda)$ are inflated with radical acting by zero; $\Delta_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_B E(\lambda)$ has simple head $L(\lambda)$ and lies in the Serre subcategory $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$; the ordinary Verma surjects onto it. Duality preserves the subcategory and $\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ embeds in the ordinary dual Verma.

[F2] Ordinary category-$\mathcal O$ structure ([[def-bgg-category-o]], [[def-verma-module]], [[thm-category-o-is-abelian-and-extension-closed]], [[thm-category-o-has-enough-projectives]], [[prop-projective-covers-in-o-are-indecomposable-and-unique]], [[thm-every-category-o-object-has-finite-length]], [[lem-finite-length-objects-decompose-into-indecomposables]], [[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]], [[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]]): enough projectives, finite length and weight spaces, simple highest-weight objects, essential projective covers, and finite direct-sum decompositions.

[F3] Ordinary weights and orthogonality ([[prop-weights-of-a-verma-module-lie-below-lambda]], [[thm-universal-property-of-verma-modules]], [[lem-standard-costandard-hom-and-ext-vanishing]]): ordinary Verma weights lie in $\lambda-Q^+$; a highest-weight vector generates a quotient of that Verma; ordinary standard-costandard Hom is $\delta_{\lambda\mu}\mathbb C$. Here $Q^+$ is the nonnegative integral simple-root cone; its strict root order is transitive.

[F4] Levi splitting and PBW ([[thm-weyls-complete-reducibility-theorem]], [[thm-finite-dimensional-simple-modules-are-classified-by-dominant-highest-weights]], [[thm-pbw-ordered-monomial-basis-for-the-enveloping-algebra]]): finite-dimensional $\mathfrak h$-semisimple Levi modules split into simples, since the center splits into weight spaces and the derived Levi is semisimple; $U(\mathfrak g)=N\otimes B$ by PBW; $N$ has nonpositive $\zeta$-degrees, $N_0=\mathbb C$ and finite-dimensional homogeneous pieces.

[F5] Central summands ([[thm-category-o-decomposes-by-generalized-central-character]], [[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]], [[lem-dominant-weights-are-maxima-of-their-weyl-orbits]]): projection to a central-character summand is exact; the labels in an integral summand lie in a finite dot-Weyl orbit with a dot-dominant representative $\kappa$, and $\lambda\le\kappa$ for every label.

[F6] Restricted duality ([[prop-restricted-duality-is-an-exact-involution-on-category-o]]) is exact, simple-preserving and involutive, exchanges ordinary standards and costandards, and preserves the parabolic subcategory. Projectivity and injectivity have their represented-Hom meaning ([[def-projective-object]], [[def-injective-object]]). The Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) is inherited and used for bases, maximal kernels, splittings and the indicated covers and lifts.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Simples and standards.** By [F1], Levi-dominant integral highest weights are exactly the simple labels in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$. Their generalized standards are quotients of the ordinary Vermas with the same one-dimensional highest-weight space and simple head. They have finite length by [F2], and their weights, and hence highest weights of composition factors, lie in $\lambda-Q^+$ by [F3]. For any parabolic quotient of the ordinary Verma, the image of its highest vector is killed by the full positive nilpotent algebra. Its finite Levi span is the cyclic highest-weight simple $E(\lambda)$ by complete reducibility, and the radical kills that span since it kills the highest vector and is Levi-stable. The induction universal property therefore factors the quotient map through $\Delta_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$. This proves the largest-quotient assertion locally. This proves parts (1) and (2). [F1, F2, F3, F4]

1.2 **Largest locally finite quotient.** For $M\in\mathcal O$, let $\mathcal K$ be the set of its subobjects $K$ such that $M/K\in\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$. It contains $M$, and finite length bounds $\ell(M/K)$, so choose $K_0$ for which this quotient length is maximal. For every $K\in\mathcal K$, the diagonal map embeds $M/(K\cap K_0)$ in $M/K\oplus M/K_0$. Serre closure gives $K\cap K_0\in\mathcal K$. Maximality and the epimorphism $M/(K\cap K_0)\to M/K_0$ force equality of lengths; its kernel is therefore zero and $K_0\subseteq K$. Thus $K_0$ is the least kernel among all parabolic quotients. For a map $M\to V$ with $V$ parabolic, its image is parabolic and its kernel lies in $\mathcal K$, so the map factors uniquely through $M/K_0$. This proves the functorial universal property of $L_{\mathfrak p}M=M/K_0$ and its left adjunction to the exact inclusion. It is right exact as a left adjoint. [F1, F2, F6, algebra]

1.3 **The correct Hom arrows.** The ordinary Verma surjection is $M(\eta)\twoheadrightarrow\Delta_{\mathfrak p}(\eta)$, and the costandard inclusion is $\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\xi)\hookrightarrow DM(\xi)$. Composing with these maps injects parabolic $\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_{\mathfrak p}(\eta),\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\xi))$ into the ordinary standard-costandard Hom of [F3]. Thus it is zero for different labels and at most one-dimensional for equal labels. In the equal case the nonzero composite through $L(\eta)$ is a homomorphism from the standard head to the costandard socle, so its dimension is one. [F1, F3, F6, algebra]

1.4 **Every parabolic standard-costandard extension splits.** Consider $0\to\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\xi)\to X\to\Delta_{\mathfrak p}(\eta)\to0$. First suppose $\xi-\eta\notin Q^+\setminus\{0\}$, including equality and incomparability. Choose a weight-$\eta$ lift $v$ of the source highest vector. If a positive root vector sent $v$ nontrivially to weight $\eta+\alpha$, its image in the standard quotient would be zero, so this weight would occur in the costandard. But all costandard weights are $\le\xi$; hence $\eta<\eta+\alpha\le\xi$ would imply $\eta<\xi$, contrary to the case assumption. Thus $v$ is killed by every positive root vector. Its Levi span is finite dimensional because $X$ is locally parabolic-finite. By [F4] it is the cyclic finite Levi highest-weight simple $E(\eta)$: complete reducibility decomposes the span, and the nonzero components of a highest-weight vector of weight $\eta$ belong to copies of that same simple, with cyclic diagonal span one copy. The radical kills this whole span since it kills $v$ and $[\mathfrak l,\mathfrak u]\subseteq\mathfrak u$. Induction therefore gives a map $\Delta_{\mathfrak p}(\eta)\to X$ whose composite onto the quotient is the identity on its generating top, hence the identity. The extension splits. In the remaining case $\eta<\xi$, duality gives an extension with reversed pair $(\xi,\eta)$, to which the first case applies; dualizing the splitting back finishes the proof. Consequently parabolic $\operatorname{Ext}^1(\Delta_{\mathfrak p}(\eta),\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\xi))=0$ for every pair, proved inside this category. The argument uses the absence of a weight obtained by raising the chosen top, not a total ordering of incomparable highest weights. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F6, algebra]

1.5 **Finite bounded projectives in an integral summand.** Fix such a central-character summand $\chi$, with dot-dominant $\kappa$ from [F5]. Every weight of every object in it is $\le\kappa$, because its composition factors have highest labels in that dot orbit. The grading element has nonnegative value on $Q^+$, so every $\zeta$-weight is at most $\kappa(\zeta)$. For a parabolic label $\eta$ put $d=\kappa(\zeta)-\eta(\zeta)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ and let $E=E(\eta)$. Define the finite-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-module $B_{\le d}(E)$ by inducing $E$ from the Levi to $\mathfrak p$ and quotienting by all positive-radical PBW terms of $\zeta$-degree greater than $d$. These terms form a submodule since the Levi preserves degree and the radical increases it. On every object $W$ in the summand, a Levi map $E\to W$ automatically kills the excluded terms after extension to $U(\mathfrak p)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak l)}E$, as their weights exceed the bound. The descending radical-degree filtration of this finite module has semisimple Levi slices killed by the radical; exact PBW induction gives a finite generalized-standard flag and places its induction in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ before central projection. Thus $Q(E)=\operatorname{pr}_\chi(U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_B B_{\le d}(E))$ represents $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak l}(E,W)$. This functor is exact: lift a basis of any finite Levi image through an epimorphism, take the finite sum of the Levi spans of those lifts, and split the resulting finite Levi epimorphism by [F4]. Hence $Q(E)$ is projective in this summand and maps onto $L(\eta)$. [F1, F2, F4, F5, F6, algebra]

2.1 **Projective covers and enough projectives.** The adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}}(L_{\mathfrak p}P,-)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,-)$ on the parabolic subcategory, so an ordinary projective has parabolic projective image. For a parabolic simple $L(\lambda)$, apply $L_{\mathfrak p}$ to the ordinary projective cover to obtain $L_{\mathfrak p}P^{(\mathcal O)}(\lambda)\twoheadrightarrow L(\lambda)$. If a subobject of this image surjects onto the simple, its inverse image in the ordinary cover does also and is the whole cover by essentiality. Hence the image map is essential and is the required parabolic projective cover. An ordinary projective epimorphism onto any parabolic object becomes a parabolic projective epimorphism by right exactness. Dualizing gives enough injectives. This proves part (3) on all the objects in the stated parabolic category. [F1, F2, F6, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 **These projectives begin with actual PBW flags.** Filter $B_{\le d}(E)$ by descending radical degree. Each degree slice is finite-dimensional and semisimple for the Levi, with radical acting by zero on the slice. PBW makes induction from $B$ exact, so inducing this filtration gives a finite generalized-standard flag on $U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_B B_{\le d}(E)$. A generalized standard has scalar central character, because its ordinary Verma precursor does; exact central projection therefore either retains or kills each whole standard slice. Hence $Q(E)$ has an actual finite generalized-standard flag. As an $N$-module the unprojected induction is graded free of finite rank, with basis the finite graded space $B_{\le d}(E)$. Central projection is an $N$-linear grading-preserving direct-summand projection. Every parabolic projective cover in the chosen summand is a grading-preserving summand of the corresponding $Q(E)$: lift the epimorphism $Q(E)\to L(\eta)$ to its cover, use essentiality for surjectivity, then split by projectivity. [F1, F2, F4, F5, step 2.1, step 1.5, algebra]

4.1 **Graded direct summands stay free.** For a graded $N$-module bounded above, the equality $V=N_{<0}V$ forces $V=0$: a nonzero homogeneous component of highest occupied degree cannot be obtained from strictly higher-degree components. Let $R$ be a grading-preserving direct summand of a finite graded free $N$-module. Then $R/N_{<0}R$ is finite dimensional. Choose a homogeneous basis of this quotient and lifts to $R$, giving a map from a finite graded free module $G$ onto $R$; its cokernel is bounded above and equals its own $N_{<0}$ multiple, so the map is surjective by the preceding argument. It splits as a graded $N$-map since $R$ is a graded projective summand. The kernel $K$ then has $K/N_{<0}K=0$, because the induced map on generator quotients is an isomorphism and reduction of the split sequence is split exact. The same bounded-above argument gives $K=0$. Thus $R$ is graded free of finite rank. This proves the summand claim without importing the flag criterion or assuming finite-dimensional degree-zero pieces of an enveloping Levi algebra. [F4, F6, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 **Free finite rank gives generalized-standard flags.** Let $R$ be one of these parabolic $\mathfrak g$-modules, graded free of finite $N$-rank. Within its fixed $\zeta$-eigenvalue coset its degrees are bounded above and its components finite dimensional. Let $a$ be its highest occupied degree. The finite Levi module $R_a$ is semisimple and the positive radical kills it, as it raises degree. A homogeneous free basis shows that all its degree-$a$ basis vectors are part of an $N$-basis, so the induction map $U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_B R_a=N\otimes R_a\to R$ is injective and its quotient is again graded free, with those finitely many generators removed. Decomposing $R_a$ into finite Levi simples gives an actual submodule that is a finite sum of generalized standards. Repeating on the quotient terminates since each step reduces the finite $N$-rank. All subobjects and quotients lie in the selected central summand; hence their simple Levi labels are the allowed labels there. This proves that every projective cover, and therefore every finite sum and summand of them, has a finite generalized-standard flag. The grading is only the actual semisimple $\zeta$-action, shifted on its coset; it is not a Koszul assumption. This proves the flag part of (4). [F1, F2, F4, F5, step 3.1, step 4.1, induction]

6.1 **Reciprocity.** For a generalized-standard flag of $P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$, steps 1.3 and 1.4 make $\operatorname{Hom}(-,\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))$ exact along its flag sequences and show that its dimension counts precisely the $\Delta_{\mathfrak p}(\mu)$ sections. On the other hand projectivity makes $\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda),-)$ exact along a composition series of $\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\mu)$. Its value on a simple has dimension one for $L(\lambda)$ and zero for every other label, by the essential simple head of the projective cover. Consequently $(P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):\Delta_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=[\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\mu):L(\lambda)]=[\Delta_{\mathfrak p}(\mu):L(\lambda)]$, the last equality by simple-preserving duality. This also proves independence of flag multiplicities and their finiteness. By standard support, only $\mu\ge\lambda$ occurs, and the diagonal multiplicity is one. [F1, F2, F6, step 2.1, step 1.3, step 1.4, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 **Labelled standard quotient and its higher-standard kernel.** The same lifting argument as in step 1.4, with $\Delta_{\mathfrak p}(\beta)$ in place of the costandard, shows $\operatorname{Ext}^1(\Delta_{\mathfrak p}(\alpha),\Delta_{\mathfrak p}(\beta))=0$ whenever $\alpha\not<\beta$: its submodule has no weight strictly above the lifted top $\alpha$, and finite Levi splitting supplies the section. In the flag of $P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ from step 5.1, the labelled standard occurs once and every other standard has strictly higher label by step 6.1. Whenever the labelled standard precedes a higher standard in the flag, the corresponding two-section subquotient splits by this Ext vanishing. Swapping those two sections moves the labelled standard upwards in the flag; finitely many swaps place it last. Thus there is an actual epimorphism $P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)\to\Delta_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ with a kernel having a finite flag of strictly higher standards. This is the highest-weight projective-kernel axiom, obtained without the tilting or homological-criterion suppliers. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.4, step 5.1, step 6.1, algebra]

8.1 **Bases, characters and conclusion.** In the fixed integral summand there are finitely many allowed labels by [F5]. Their simple classes form its finite-length Grothendieck basis; the standard-to-simple matrix has diagonal one and entries only below the diagonal after a linear extension of the root order. It is therefore invertible over $\mathbb Z$, so standard classes give another basis. A finite relation between the simple characters has a maximal highest-weight label with a nonzero coefficient; its highest-weight monomial occurs in that simple with coefficient one and in no remaining incomparable or lower simple, so the relation cannot vanish. Inducting proves that characters are injective on this Grothendieck group. The constructions above establish the simples and standard support, the reflector and enough projectives, the local Hom/Ext orthogonality, actual generalized-standard flags, reciprocity and the labelled higher-standard kernel. Duality has remained the ordinary restricted duality restricted to the actual parabolic subcategory. These are all four parts of the Statement. [F1, F2, F5, F6, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 1.3, step 1.4, step 5.1, step 6.1, step 7.1] ∎

## Remarks

This proof constructs the generalized-standard projective flags by finite graded PBW and Levi splitting, including the Levi center. It uses neither the homological flag criterion nor tilting classification, and does not apply the merely right-exact reflector to an ordinary Verma flag.

Connectedness is not required. Write $(\Lambda,\preceq)$ for its label poset, $L_\lambda$ for its simples, $\Delta_\lambda$ for its generalized standards, and $\nabla_\lambda=D\Delta_\lambda$ for its costandards. The duality $D$ is exact, contravariant and simple-preserving.

The projective cover $P_\lambda$ and injective envelope $I_\lambda=DP_\lambda$ have exact sequences
$$0\longrightarrow K_\lambda\longrightarrow P_\lambda\longrightarrow\Delta_\lambda\longrightarrow0,\qquad0\longrightarrow\nabla_\lambda\longrightarrow I_\lambda\longrightarrow C_\lambda\longrightarrow0,$$
where $K_\lambda$ has a finite standard flag with labels strictly greater than $\lambda$, and $C_\lambda=DK_\lambda$ has a finite costandard flag with such labels. Generally $I_\lambda$ is larger than $\nabla_\lambda$. Standards have simple heads, costandards simple socles, and their composition labels are $\preceq\lambda$. In this split setting,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=\delta_{\lambda\mu}\mathbb C,\qquad\operatorname{Ext}^j(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=0\quad(j>0),$$
and BGG reciprocity is $(P_\lambda:\Delta_\mu)=[\nabla_\mu:L_\lambda]=[\Delta_\mu:L_\lambda]$. Higher Ext vanishing is justified below from the standard-kernel sequences and the local Hom/$\operatorname{Ext}^1$ statement.

A **finite standard flag** of $N$ is a finite chain $0=N_0\subset N_1\subset\cdots\subset N_r=N$ with sections $\Delta_{\lambda_i}$; a **finite costandard flag** has sections $\nabla_{\lambda_i}$. The zero object has the empty flag. Write $\mathcal F(\Delta)$ and $\mathcal F(\nabla)$ for the corresponding full subcategories. They are exact categories with the short exact sequences inherited from $\mathcal C$, closed under finite sums, extensions and direct summands. Their flag multiplicities are independent of the chosen flag and satisfy
$$(N:\Delta_\lambda)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(N,\nabla_\lambda),\qquad(M:\nabla_\lambda)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\lambda,M).$$
For arbitrary objects of the fixed finite summand, the equivalent homological criteria are
$$\mathcal F(\Delta)=\{N:\operatorname{Ext}^1(N,\nabla_\lambda)=0\text{ for all }\lambda\}=\{N:\operatorname{Ext}^j(N,\nabla_\lambda)=0\text{ for all }\lambda,j>0\},$$
$$\mathcal F(\nabla)=\{M:\operatorname{Ext}^1(\Delta_\lambda,M)=0\text{ for all }\lambda\}=\{M:\operatorname{Ext}^j(\Delta_\lambda,M)=0\text{ for all }\lambda,j>0\}.$$
The duality exchanges the two flag categories. A **tilting object** belongs to their intersection.

An indecomposable tilting object is **normalized at** $\lambda$, and written $T_\lambda$, if it has an inclusion $\Delta_\lambda\hookrightarrow T_\lambda$ whose cokernel is standard-filtered by labels strictly smaller than $\lambda$. Its bottom standard occurs once and $\lambda$ is its unique maximal composition-support label. Such an object, when it exists, is unique up to isomorphism. Existence and classification are supplied later; they are not used to prove the criteria. For a lower ideal $\Gamma$ containing $\lambda$, this same object is normalized tilting in the corresponding Serre subcategory; it is unchanged by the truncation.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The finite split highest-weight central summand $\mathcal C$ over $\mathbb C$, the labels and structural objects above, and its finite-dimensional basic block algebra $A$, whose finite-dimensional left modules model $\mathcal C$.

[F1] Highest-weight structure ([[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]): finite labels and length, finite-dimensional Hom, standard support $[\Delta_\lambda:L_\mu]\ne0\Rightarrow\mu\preceq\lambda$, diagonal multiplicity one, projective covers, standard-kernel sequences with strictly higher flags, BGG reciprocity, and $\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=\delta_{\lambda\mu}\mathbb C$ and $\operatorname{Ext}^1(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=0$ inside the parabolic category.

[F2] The flag terminology agrees with the ordinary category-$\mathcal O$ terminology ([[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]], [[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]], [[thm-bgg-reciprocity]], [[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]], [[cor-injectives-have-costandard-filtrations]], [[thm-every-category-o-object-has-finite-length]]). The argument here uses the actual generalized-standard structure in [F1].

[F3] Restricted BGG duality ([[prop-restricted-duality-is-an-exact-involution-on-category-o]]) restricts to an exact contravariant involution of this summand, fixes simples and sends $\Delta_\lambda$ to $\nabla_\lambda$ and $P_\lambda$ to $I_\lambda$.

[F4] In the split basic algebra model, primitive idempotents $e_\lambda$ give $P_\lambda=Ae_\lambda$ and $\dim e_\lambda N=[N:L_\lambda]$. A projective generator is the finite sum of the projective covers; its endomorphism algebra is finite dimensional by [F1]. All modules and multiplicity spaces used below are finite dimensional over $\mathbb C$.

[F5] The Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) is available when choosing bases, lifts, projective resolutions and injective cogenerators; no stronger field or nonsplit division-algebra assertion is made.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Flags, duality and the injective sequence.** Finite sums have flags by concatenation. Given $0\to X\to Y\to Z\to0$ with $X,Z$ standard-filtered, pull a flag of $Z$ back to $Y$ and precede it with the flag of $X$; this gives a standard flag of $Y$. Duality proves both claims for costandard flags and exchanges the two flag categories. Dualizing $0\to K_\lambda\to P_\lambda\to\Delta_\lambda\to0$ gives precisely $0\to\nabla_\lambda\to I_\lambda\to DK_\lambda\to0$, whose cokernel is costandard-filtered by labels strictly above $\lambda$. In particular this construction does not identify a general costandard with an injective envelope. [F1, F2, F3]

2.1 **All positive standard-costandard Ext groups.** The degree-one vanishing is [F1]. Suppose vanishing holds in degree $j-1$ for every pair of structural labels, where $j\ge2$. A finite standard flag of $K_\lambda$ and its long exact sequences give $\operatorname{Ext}^{j-1}(K_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=0$. The projective sequence then gives $\operatorname{Ext}^{j}(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^{j-1}(K_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=0$. Induction proves all positive degrees. Filtering the first variable now shows $\operatorname{Ext}^{j}(N,\nabla_\mu)=0$ for any standard-filtered $N$; filtering the second variable gives the dual statement for costandard-filtered objects, and also vanishing between any standard-filtered and costandard-filtered pair. [F1, step 1.1, induction]

2.2 **The maximal trace.** Choose a maximal label $\eta$ and put $e=e_\eta$. Since the standard-kernel sequence has no higher labels, $Ae=P_\eta=\Delta_\eta$. Every other standard is killed by $e$, while $\dim e\Delta_\eta=1$. An endomorphism of $\Delta_\eta$ is determined by its action on the generating top space, so $eAe=\operatorname{End}_A(Ae)^{\mathrm{op}}=\mathbb C$. For a standard-filtered $X$, the evaluation map $Ae\otimes_{\mathbb C}eX\to X$ is injective and its quotient is standard-filtered with no $\eta$ section. To prove this, induct on a chosen flag. If its last section is $\Delta_\eta$, the section splits off because $\Delta_\eta$ is projective. If its last section is another $\Delta_\lambda$, it is killed by $e$, so $eX=eX'$ for the preceding flag subobject $X'$ and the trace lies in $X'$; the induction quotient extends by $\Delta_\lambda$. This proves the claim in both cases, including identification with the canonical trace generated by $eX$. [F1, F4, F5, step 1.1, induction]

3.1 **Multiplicity formulas.** For $0\to N'\to N\to\Delta_\lambda\to0$ with $N'$ standard-filtered, applying $\operatorname{Hom}(-,\nabla_\mu)$ and step 2.1 gives a short exact sequence of Hom spaces. Its dimension adds one precisely for $\lambda=\mu$. Inducting along a flag proves $(N:\Delta_\mu)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(N,\nabla_\mu)$ and independence of the flag. Duality gives $(M:\nabla_\mu)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\mu,M)$ for costandard-filtered $M$. [F1, F3, step 2.1, induction]

3.2 **The genuine heredity ideal.** Apply step 2.2 to each projective column $Ae_\lambda$ and sum the columns. The resulting injective evaluation map is multiplication $Ae\otimes_{eAe}eA\to A$, with image $J=AeA$. Thus $J\cong Ae\otimes_{\mathbb C}eA$, rather than $J=Ae$. It is projective on both sides: on the left it is a finite sum of $Ae$, and on the right a finite sum of $eA$. Moreover $e\operatorname{rad}(A)e=0$ since $eAe=\mathbb C$, so $J$ is a heredity ideal. Put $A'=A/J$. The finite $A'$-modules are exactly the $A$-modules killed by $e$, hence the Serre subcategory on $\Lambda\setminus\{\eta\}$. Its projective covers for $\lambda\ne\eta$ are $A'e_\lambda=Ae_\lambda/J e_\lambda$. By step 2.2 these have standard flags with all $\eta$ sections removed. The sequence onto $\Delta_\lambda$ has kernel $K_\lambda/J e_\lambda$: the trace $J e_\lambda$ lies in $K_\lambda$ because $e\Delta_\lambda=0$, and applying step 2.2 to $K_\lambda$ gives the required standard flag with the remaining strictly higher labels. Its simple top is still $L_\lambda$, so it is indeed the projective cover. Consequently $A'$ has the smaller highest-weight structure with unchanged standards $\Delta_\lambda$. Duality preserves this Serre subcategory and gives its injective envelopes and unchanged costandards $\nabla_\lambda$. Every injective $A'$-module is therefore costandard-filtered by these smaller labels. This establishes the quotient data needed for induction, without assuming the converse flag criterion. [F1, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 2.2, algebra]

3.3 **Normalized tilting uniqueness.** Suppose $X,X'$ are indecomposable tiltings with normalized inclusions $i:\Delta_\lambda\to X$ and $i':\Delta_\lambda\to X'$. Their cokernels are standard-filtered, so step 2.1 gives $\operatorname{Ext}^1(X/\Delta_\lambda,X')=0$. The Hom exact sequence extends $i'$ to $f:X\to X'$ with $fi=i'$; symmetrically obtain $g:X'\to X$ with $gi'=i$. Then $gf$ and $fg$ restrict to the identity on the common nonzero standard, and no positive power of either is zero. In a finite-dimensional endomorphism algebra of an indecomposable finite-length object, Fitting's decomposition makes every noninvertible endomorphism nilpotent. Hence both composites are invertible and $f$ is an isomorphism. The support of $\Delta_\lambda$ and of the lower-labelled quotient shows that $\lambda$ is the unique maximal support label. No existence or tilting classification was used in the flag-criterion argument. [F1, F4, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 **Ext1 implies every positive Ext degree.** Suppose $N$ satisfies $\operatorname{Ext}^1_A(N,\nabla_\lambda)=0$ for every label. Finite flags show $\operatorname{Ext}^1_A(N,C)=0$ for every costandard-filtered $C$. More generally, if the groups vanish in degree $j-1$ against all costandards, they vanish in that degree against every costandard-filtered object. Apply this to $C_\lambda$ in the actual sequence $0\to\nabla_\lambda\to I_\lambda\to C_\lambda\to0$ from step 1.1. Since $I_\lambda$ is injective, for $j\ge2$ dimension shifting gives $\operatorname{Ext}^j_A(N,\nabla_\lambda)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^{j-1}_A(N,C_\lambda)=0$. Induction establishes all positive Ext vanishing, and filtering establishes $\operatorname{Ext}^j_A(N,I')=0$ for every $j>0$ and every injective $A'$-module $I'$ from step 3.2, viewed as an $A$-module. [step 1.1, step 3.2, induction]

5.1 **Tor vanishing detected by injectives.** Choose a projective resolution $P_\bullet\to N$ by finite-dimensional projective $A$-modules. Each $A'\otimes_A P_i$ is projective over $A'$. For an injective $A'$-module $I'$, tensor-Hom adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{A'}(A'\otimes_A P_\bullet,I')$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_A(P_\bullet,I')$. The latter has zero cohomology in every positive degree by step 4.1. Because $\operatorname{Hom}_{A'}(-,I')$ is exact, the degree-$j$ cohomology of the former is $\operatorname{Hom}_{A'}(H_j(A'\otimes_A P_\bullet),I')$. Injectives detect nonzero finite-dimensional $A'$-modules: embed the semisimple socle of a finite module in a finite sum of the injective envelopes of the simples and extend the map by injectivity. Its kernel is zero because any nonzero finite-length submodule intersects that socle. Thus the full module embeds in such an injective cogenerator. It follows that $H_j(A'\otimes_A P_\bullet)=\operatorname{Tor}^A_j(A',N)=0$ for every $j>0$. This uses actual homology detection, not an assumed exactness of tensoring. [F4, F5, step 3.2, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 **The trace exact sequence and quotient induction.** Tensor $0\to J\to A\to A'\to0$ with $N$. By step 5.1 its Tor boundary vanishes, and step 3.2 identifies the result as $0\to Ae\otimes_{\mathbb C}eN\to N\to E\to0$, where $E=A'\otimes_A N$. The kernel is a finite sum of $\Delta_\eta$. Moreover $A'\otimes_A P_\bullet$ is a projective resolution of $E$ by step 5.1, and adjunction now gives $\operatorname{Ext}^j_{A'}(E,\nabla_\lambda)=\operatorname{Ext}^j_A(N,\nabla_\lambda)=0$ for $j>0$, $\lambda\ne\eta$. Induct on the number of labels, using the smaller highest-weight category constructed in step 3.2: $E$ is standard-filtered by the smaller labels. The base with no labels is the zero category; with one label the trace sequence itself is $N\cong\Delta_\eta\otimes eN$. Extension closure now makes $N$ standard-filtered. Together with steps 2.1 and 4.1 this proves both displayed standard-flag criteria, using either degree-one or all-positive-Ext vanishing. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.2, step 4.1, step 5.1, induction]

7.1 **The dual criterion and direct summands.** Exact contravariant duality gives $\operatorname{Ext}^j_A(\Delta_\lambda,M)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^j_A(DM,\nabla_\lambda)$ by reversing Yoneda extensions (and likewise in all degrees). The criterion for $DM$ in step 6.1 therefore gives the two costandard-flag criteria for $M$. If a flagged object is a finite direct sum, Ext groups of each summand are direct summands of its vanishing groups. The appropriate criterion shows every summand has the same kind of flag. Thus both flag categories, and their intersection of tilting objects, have all the stated closure properties. [F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 6.1, algebra]

8.1 **Lower ideals.** Let $X$ be a normalized tilting object at $\lambda$, and let $\Gamma$ be a lower ideal containing $\lambda$. Every composition label of $X$ lies below $\lambda$, so $X$ belongs to its Serre subcategory. Its standard flag uses labels in $\Gamma$; every costandard occurring in its costandard flag also has its own labelled simple as a composition factor of $X$, hence has label in $\Gamma$. These are the same standards and costandards in the truncated highest-weight category: iteratively removing maximal labels outside $\Gamma$ uses step 3.2. Thus $X$ remains the same normalized tilting there, and uniqueness follows from step 3.3. The closure, duality, multiplicity and full homological-criterion assertions have been established locally, including the genuine injective and heredity-ideal interfaces. [F1, F3, step 1.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 6.1, step 7.1, step 3.3] ∎
